subject: Linguistics
title: The Greek Alphabet
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Greek Alphabet usable.

hook.text: Greeks borrowed the Phoenician abjad around 800 BCE—but made one crucial change: they added vowels.

buildup.text: Phoenician consonant letters with no Greek equivalent were repurposed as vowel symbols.

discovery.text: Phoenician 'aleph' (a glottal stop) became Greek 'alpha' (the vowel A)—the first true alphabet was born.

twist.text: Adding vowels made the script usable for any language—not just those where context fills vowel gaps.

climax.text: The Greek alphabet begat Latin in the west and Cyrillic in the east—two branches of one tree.

punchline.text: Adding vowels turned a good script into a universal one.

quiz.question: What innovation did the Greeks add to the Phoenician script?
